```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(multcomp)
library(forcats)
mortality <- read.csv("Adult mortality rate (2019-2021).csv")

mort_cv <-  mortality|> #31 observations per fold so trainging data will have 124 observations
  mutate(
    fold = sample(rep(1:5, length.out = n()))
  )

mort_cv <- mort_cv|>
    dplyr::rename(avg_pop = Average_Pop.thousands.people.)  # Average Population per 1000 people

colnames(mort_cv)[4] <- "avg_gdp"
colnames(mort_cv)[6] <- "avg_hexp"
```

```{r}
#model with indicator functions
mort_lm <- lm(Average_CDR ~ fct_relevel(Continent, "North America") + fct_relevel(Development_level, "short") + avg_pop + avg_hexp, data = mort_cv)

print(summary(mort_lm))

#model with indicator functions & interactions
mort_lm_int <- lm(Average_CDR ~ fct_relevel(Continent, "North America") + fct_relevel(Development_level, "short") + avg_pop + avg_hexp + fct_relevel(Development_level, "short")*avg_pop + fct_relevel(Development_level, "short")*avg_hexp + fct_relevel(Continent, "North America")*avg_pop + fct_relevel(Continent, "North America")*avg_hexp , data = mort_cv)
```

```{r}
#anova test to determine whether interactions improve the model

anova(mort_lm, mort_lm_int)

#low p-value 0.001199 so we reject the null hypothesis that the models are the same. 
```

```{r}
plot(mort_lm_int, which = 1) #fitted vs residuals plot
plot(mort_lm_int, which = 2) # qq plot looks mostly normal with a little right skew
shapiro.test(residuals(mort_lm_int)) # p-value is 0.3231 which fail to reject Ho that the distribution's residulas are is non-normal
hist(residuals(mort_lm_int))# histogra of residuals looks normally distributed

plot(mort_lm_int, which = 5)#Residuals vs leverage
plot(mort_lm_int, which = 3)# Scale-Location
plot(mort_lm_int, which = 4)# cook's distance
```

```{r}
library(forcats)
# Loads forcats, which provides fct_relevel(). Not strictly needed for this code,
# but your model formula uses it, so it's harmless to keep.

n <- nobs(mort_lm_int)
# n = number of observations actually used to fit the model
# (rows dropped for missing values are not counted).

p <- sum(!is.na(coef(mort_lm_int)))
# p = number of estimated coefficients, including the intercept.
# coef() returns all coefficients; is.na() marks any R couldn't estimate
# (e.g., empty interaction combinations); !is.na() flips that, and sum()
# counts the TRUEs. So p counts only real, estimated parameters.

used_rows <- as.numeric(rownames(model.frame(mort_lm_int)))
# model.frame() returns the exact data the model used, after dropping NAs.
# rownames() pulls their original row labels from mort_cv, and as.numeric()
# turns those labels into numbers so they can be used to index mort_cv.

lev_df <- data.frame(
# Builds a table with one row per observation used in the model.

  row         = used_rows,
  # Original row number in mort_cv, so you can locate each observation.

  Continent   = mort_cv$Continent[used_rows],
  # The observation's continent, pulled from the original data.

  Development = mort_cv$Development_level[used_rows],
  # The observation's development level.

  avg_pop     = mort_cv$avg_pop[used_rows],
  # The observation's average population (a predictor).

  avg_hexp    = mort_cv$avg_hexp[used_rows],
  # The observation's average health expenditure (a predictor).

  hat         = hatvalues(mort_lm_int),
  # Leverage: how unusual the observation's predictor values are (ranges 0 to 1).

  stud        = rstudent(mort_lm_int),
  # Studentized residual: how far the observed CDR is from the prediction,
  # in standard-error units, with that observation left out of the fit.

  cooksD      = cooks.distance(mort_lm_int)
  # Cook's distance: how much the fitted model changes if this observation
  # is removed. Combines leverage and residual size.
)

lev_df$high_lev  <- lev_df$hat > 2 * p / n
# TRUE if leverage exceeds the common 2p/n cutoff.

lev_df$big_resid <- abs(lev_df$stud) > 2
# TRUE if the studentized residual is beyond ±2 (an unusually poor fit).
# abs() catches both large positive and large negative residuals.

lev_df$high_cook <- lev_df$cooksD > 4 / n
# TRUE if Cook's distance exceeds the 4/n rule of thumb (potentially influential).

flagged <- subset(lev_df, high_lev | big_resid | high_cook)
# Keeps only rows that fail at least one check. "|" means OR.

flagged[order(-flagged$hat), ]
# Prints the flagged rows sorted from highest to lowest leverage.
# order() sorts ascending, so the minus sign reverses it. The empty spot
# after the comma means "keep all columns."
```

```{r}
degrees <- c(2, 4, 6, 10, 15)

grouped_cv_ns <- function(df) {
  fold_results <- map_dfr(1:5, function(f) {
    train <- filter(mort_cv, fold != f)
    test  <- filter(mort_cv, fold == f)

    fit <- lm(
      Average_CDR ~ ns(avg_pop, df = df),
      data = train
    )

    tibble(
      fold = f,
      rmse = sqrt(mean((test$avg_hexp - predict(fit, test))^2))
    )
  })

  summarise(
    fold_results,
    df = df,
    mean_rmse = mean(rmse),
    se_rmse = sd(rmse) / sqrt(n())
  )
}

fold_results <- map_dfr(degrees, function(d){
  grouped_cv_ns(df = d)
}
)
fold_results
```
